questions.stem: The President of India is ELECTED by:

options.option_text: An electoral college (elected MPs + elected MLAs of all States + Delhi & Puducherry)

questions.explanation: Indirect election — Electoral College of elected MPs (both houses) + elected MLAs of all states + NCT of Delhi + Puducherry. System of proportional representation via single transferable vote (Art 54-55). Nominated MPs / MLAs do NOT vote. Value of each vote is weighted by state population (1971 census, frozen by 84th Amendment).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The President of India can HOLD OFFICE for:

options.option_text: 5 years, eligible for re-election (no term limit)

questions.explanation: Art 56 — 5-year term. Eligible for any number of re-elections (no formal limit, though only Rajendra Prasad has served 2 consecutive terms, 1952-57 and 1957-62). Resigns by writing to Vice-President. Can be impeached for 'violation of the Constitution' under Art 61.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The MINIMUM AGE to be eligible for President of India is:
questions.explanation: Art 58 — qualifications: citizen of India, 35+, qualified for election to Lok Sabha, not holding office of profit under government. 25 = Lok Sabha MP. 30 = Rajya Sabha MP.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: A PRESIDENTIAL VETO where the President just SITS ON a bill (neither signing nor rejecting) is called:
questions.explanation: Three types available to Indian President: (1) Absolute veto — not assenting (rare, 1991 used on salary bill by Zail Singh). (2) Suspensive veto — returning for reconsideration (Art 111 — only for non-money bills); if Parliament re-passes, must sign. (3) Pocket veto — no time limit, keeps indefinitely; Zail Singh used this on the Indian Post Office (Amendment) Bill, 1986 — never signed.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The President is IMPEACHED under Article:
questions.explanation: Art 61 — impeachment for 'violation of the Constitution'. Procedure: charge by either house (2/3 special majority), investigation, then passage by other house (2/3 majority). Nominated MPs CAN participate (unique to this vote). No Indian President has been impeached. 58 — qualifications. 74 — Council of Ministers. 352 — National Emergency.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The President of India is the SUPREME COMMANDER of the:

options.option_text: Indian Armed Forces (Army + Navy + Air Force)

questions.explanation: Art 53(2) — Supreme Command of the Defence Forces of the Union is vested in the President. Exercise governed by law (functionally via Raksha Mantri and CDS). Presidential awards include Param Vir Chakra, Ashoka Chakra, etc.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Under Article 72, the President has the power to grant PARDONS. Which of these is NOT a type of pardon?
questions.explanation: Art 72 — 5 types: (1) Pardon (complete), (2) Commutation (lesser form, e.g., death to life), (3) Remission (reduction without change of kind), (4) Respite (reduced sentence due to special circumstances), (5) Reprieve (postponement). 'Annulment' is not a legal pardon category.
